name: context-first-problem-solving

name: correcting-course

Drive hub owns the canonical CORE; this copy is versioned 2026-10-16 from CORE — correcting-course.

name: learning-from-mistakes

Drive hub owns the canonical CORE; this copy is versioned 2026-10-16 from CORE — learning-from-mistakes.

name: work-preparing
description: Use when preparing work before execution (PRE) — gather enough context and constraints for a clean handoff without turning preparation into bureaucracy. Drive hub owns the canonical CORE; this copy is versioned 2026-10-06 from CORE — work-preparing.

name: proposal-drafting
description: Use when formalizing a sufficiently developed human idea into a decision-ready proposal — retrieve current state first; draft only the real delta. Drive hub owns the canonical CORE; this copy is versioned 2026-10-16 from CORE — proposal-drafting.

name: implementation-planning
description: Use when settled-enough direction needs an execution-ready path — compute the remaining implementation delta from current reality, not from the brief alone. Drive hub owns the canonical CORE; this copy is versioned 2026-10-06 from CORE — implementation-planning.

name: in-session-phasing
description: Use when the user asks to work in phases, keep the chat updating during multi-step work, or align this session with concurrent work on the same shared record.

name: citing-sources
description: Use when the user asks "where did that come from?", "cite your sources", "don't you remember?", "we discussed this", or "what do the records say?", or when consequential claims rely on files, Memory, connected systems, documents, emails, code, or web sources — retrieve and cite what actually supports each claim, never treating a failed search as absence. Drive hub owns the canonical CORE; this copy is versioned 2026-10-16 from CORE — citing-sources.

name: connective-tissue-safe-handling
description: Use when composing related facts across Drive, Notion, Slack, or Memory so relationships stay useful without flattening status, provenance, or authority. Drive hub owns the canonical CORE; this copy is versioned 2026-10-16.

name: memory-updating
description: Use when JL asks to persist, correct, replace, or forget a durable Memory fact. Drive hub owns the canonical CORE; this copy is versioned 2026-10-16 from CORE — memory-updating.

name: conversation-continuity-packaging
description: Use when packaging a conversation into durable Markdown continuity packets — on an explicit request, after an ending-session coordinator collects a Yes, or after exact "End session." confirmation — for future retrieval without carrying the whole chat. Prefer labeled museum sections (goal, decisions, constraints, facts, open, rejected) over one mushy dump. Drive hub owns the canonical CORE; this copy carries JL 2026-10-23 museum+labels.

name: library-file-processing
description: Use when turning authorized Library / box / Drive artifacts into clear, retrievable, well-placed records while preserving identity, provenance, and useful distinctions. Drive hub owns the canonical CORE; this copy is versioned 2026-10-16 from CORE — library-file-processing.

name: space-artifact-processing
description: Use when durably organizing artifacts in a persistent store (Drive folders, Notion, box files, or a ChatGPT-Space equivalent): inspect content, name, place, split/merge, preserve provenance, mutate minimally, and verify retrieval. Complements library-file-processing. Drive hub owns the canonical CORE; this copy is versioned 2026-10-16 from CORE — space-artifact-processing.

name: suggesting-prompts-and-next-steps
description: Use when JL asks for suggested prompts, follow-ups, or next steps, or when a clearly valuable continuation exists after fully answering: offer 1-3 distinct, inspectable, actionable options with full next-turn prompts. Drive hub owns the canonical CORE; this copy is versioned 2026-10-16 from CORE — suggesting-prompts-and-next-steps.

name: stripping-down-self-imposed-barriers
description: Use when an agent with a clear, authorized result is about to invent an approval gate, re-ask something already answered, swap action for a plan or relay, claim read-only against newer instructions, or stop at a draft when a verified outcome is still feasible. Drive hub owns the canonical CORE; this copy is versioned 2026-10-16 from CORE — stripping-down-self-imposed-barriers.

name: dinner-tomorrow-me
description: When JL says "dinner tomorrow me", "dumb it down", asks for fewer words or a compact visual, or a reply is turning into an essay: compress it to one at-a-glance takeaway without losing truth or required work.

name: reference-media-prompts
description: Use when writing generation prompts for reference-based image or short-form video — produce one clear affirmative production brief for the target model. Drive hub owns the canonical CORE; this copy is versioned 2026-10-16 from CORE — reference-media-prompts.

name: displaying-using-python
description: Use when the user wants existing image or video-frame pixels (crops, enlargements, frames, Python-made graphics) actually shown in chat, not just a path, link, or description. Drive hub owns the canonical CORE; this copy is versioned 2026-10-16 from CORE — displaying-using-python.

name: iui-research-panel
description: Use when the user asks for a research panel or source picker, or when their approval of which sources/scope to research is materially needed — present the 15-source selector with presets, depth (including a 21+ deep-sweep option), method, and format, then research only the submitted selection. Drive hub owns the canonical CORE; this copy is versioned 2026-10-18 from CORE — iui-research-panel.

name: clocking-in
description: Use when the user says "Clocking in" (or similar) to start or re-enter productive work in the current conversation — recover the work position, pick one eligible unit of work, execute, and verify. Drive hub owns the canonical CORE; this copy is versioned 2026-10-16 from CORE — clocking-in.

name: clocking-out
description: Use when the user says "Clocking out", "End session.", or otherwise asks to close the session — dispatch to ending-session (close with continuity packaging unless declined) without becoming a second closeout orchestrator. Drive hub owns the canonical CORE; this copy is versioned 2026-10-16 from CORE — clocking-out.

name: bumping-session
description: Use when the user returns to a conversation after a gap, asks how much time has passed, or wants to re-anchor the thread — establish a trustworthy session boundary from timestamp evidence, and resume prior work only if explicitly asked. Drive hub owns the canonical CORE; this copy is versioned 2026-10-16 from CORE — bumping-session.

name: ending-session
description: Use when the user says exactly "End session.", asks to close the session, or asks whether the session is ready to end — run the Yes/No/Other packaging-consent gate and orchestrate a verified, proportional closeout. Drive hub owns the canonical CORE; this copy is versioned 2026-10-16 from CORE — ending-session.

name: getting-dressed
description: Use when JL says get dressed, recover it, continue after a detour, or take command — retrieve missing context first, restore the working position, and resume the actual work. Drive hub owns the canonical CORE; this copy is versioned 2026-10-06 from CORE — getting-dressed.

name: auditable-actions-tracing-and-logging
description: Use when substantial work materially changes or steers something and you need a concise, evidence-grounded action log in chat without dumping process exhaust into durable sources.

name: propagating-to-internal-sources
description: Use when a decision or new fact should be carried into the internal sources that own it — discover affected records, apply authorized edits, and verify each by read-back.

name: workspace-skill-maintenance
description: Use when reviewing a workspace Skill against current reality without editing its behavior — update Last reviewed metadata only; hand behavioral drift to workspace-skill-changing-update. Drive hub owns the canonical CORE; this copy is versioned 2026-10-06 from CORE — workspace-skill-maintenance.

name: workspace-skill-changing-update
description: Use when JL has authorized a behavioral change to a workspace Skill — apply the smallest complete update via UpdateSkill and validate; not for Last reviewed-only maintenance. Drive hub owns the canonical CORE; this copy is versioned 2026-10-06 from CORE — workspace-skill-changing-update.

name: agent-bootstrap
description: Initialize an existing agent manifestation at session start, or provision missing startup guidance when it genuinely does not exist. Use at session initialization or explicit (re)initialization to resolve the active identity, load only the minimum durable guidance (identity, behavior core, user directives, operating instructions), reconcile authority and chronology, route the real task to the owning source, and continue into the user's work. Not for an already-active agent that only lost its work position (use getting-dressed).

name: communicating-effectively
description: Route and attribute AI-authored communications transparently and effectively across human-AI and AI-AI boundaries. Use when preparing, forwarding, writing, sending, posting, replying to, or correcting an agent handoff, chat or email message, operational comment, durable authored instruction, or cross-provider prompt; when choosing a communication surface or connector; or when repairing missing AI attribution. Send only with authority, keep a visible author signature inside the material, verify the real outcome, and write for a busy human reader with evidence-led status.

name: company-knowledge-routing
description: Route the next knowledge operation to the source or context that actually owns the needed information, and choose READ, WRITE, READ -> WRITE, or NONE. Use when deciding where to read or write company knowledge next (conversation, Notion, Drive, Linear, repository, database, chat, Library, public web, or another AI context) by ownership rather than convenience, when a named Skill is missing from the installed list, or when prior-decision recall needs the right starting source. Keep routing narrow and return to the parent task.

name: wrapping-up-turn
description: Provide an accurate, visually useful final checkpoint for the current turn and stop expanding the task. Use when the user asks to stop and calibrate, show what the agent has been doing before stopping, summarize its current thinking and pause, or wrap up only this response. A bare STOP means stop immediately; session-ending and clock-out requests belong to their own procedures.

name: card-preflight
description: Core skill. Use before sending the owner any question or decision card, or before starring or voting on any option: research the star first, check which options clash, choose either-or versus multi-select, put the plain question first, and send one card instead of several.
